To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) The normalized gamma activity, in multiunit recordings, falls roughly as the square-root of the number of stimuli in the scene.

the normalized gamma activity of coherent oscillations in a model feedback circuit falls roughly as the square-root-of-n in response to images containing objects of different numerosity, and that arrays of winner-take- all numerosity detectors, tuned to the normalized gamma activity within different bands, exhibit tuning curves consistent with experimental data.

the normalized gamma activity of a computer model of cortical neurons follows a square-root-of-numerosity rule, and that the normalized gamma band activity of cortical neurons may be the substrate for number- selective responses in the brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural mechanisms of visual attention.
the neural basis of numerosity perception.
the neural basis of an innate, number sense in both humans and animals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
coherent oscillations, as a general principle, could contribute to the encoding of numerosity.
the number- selectivity of the responses of cortical neurons can be derived from the coherent oscillations in the spike trains of those neurons.
coherent oscillations may contribute to the number- selective response of cortical neurons in principle, but that many critical issues await resolution. [1]
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gamma-band oscillation may be the mechanism for numerosity coding in the cortex, which is consistent with the behavioral data.
the square root law of numerosity representation is not only a fundamental law in the brain, but also an important clue for the neural representation of numerosity.
the number- selectivity of cortical neurons can be extracted from the coherent oscillations evoked in response to a scene, but that this extraction is subject to a number of limitations.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the normalized gamma activity of a multiunit spike train, which can be easily extracted from the raw data, can be a good predictor of numerosity, even in the face of considerable variability in stimulus parameters.
coherent oscillations may contribute to the numerosity information in the spike trains of cortical neurons.

the square-root-of-n law is a natural consequence of the fact that the gamma activity of an ensemble of neurons is proportional to the number of neurons in the ensemble, whereas the number of spikes is proportional to the square of the number of neurons.
